brique._comment: Engine-native Reflexive family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: vocabulary.query
objective.description: Query the root vocabulary projection under one path.

#root.role: Run a root-only vocabulary query under the requested path and return the matching child nodes.

path._comment: Optional dot-separated vocabulary path (e.g. domain.status). Empty or absent resolves the root node.

include_values._comment: Optional. When true, includes leaf values at the resolved node.

include_segments._comment: Optional. When true, includes path segment metadata.

children._comment: Child nodes at the resolved vocabulary path. Each item: { key (string — child segment name), has_children (bool — true if this node has further children), values (array of scalar values associated with this node, present only when include_values is true) }.

effects.projection_db: The root vocabulary projection is queried read-only.

transformation_contract.morphing: A root vocabulary path query becomes the list of projected child vocabulary nodes visible under that path.
invariants: vocabulary.query is root-only and operates on the derived SQLite vocabulary projection.
Returned children are ordered deterministically by kind, segment, and value fields.
include_values and include_segments filter the returned child set without mutating projection state.
success: On success, vocabulary.query returns children nodes under the resolved vocabulary parent path.
An empty children array is a valid successful result when the path exists but has no visible children after filtering.
failure: The capacity is refused outside the root context.
The capacity fails when the projection database is unavailable or when the requested path does not resolve to a vocabulary node.
notes: vocabulary.query returns child node summaries only; use vocabulary.get to retrieve the complete vocabulary document.
include_segments is accepted but does not change the external shape of child items in v1.

This queries a projection snapshot, not a live mirror of the filesystem — see meaning.rebuild's role and vocabulary.get's note on staleness. An empty or sparse children set under a path that should have content is more likely a stale/unpopulated projection than genuinely missing content; consider meaning.rebuild before concluding the world lacks what you expected.
